projects.name: Teaching Toddlers Typing
projects.problem: My toddler was learning letters but had no way to connect a letter on a keyboard to a letter on a screen — and every typing game I found punished wrong guesses, which just caused meltdowns.
projects.blurb: A dark, pearlescent typing game for toddlers: one big letter fills the screen, the child hunts for the matching physical key, and a muted celebration plays on success. Wrong keys get a soft flicker, never a penalty.

projects.name: Big Emotions
projects.problem: In the actual meltdown moment with a two-year-old, I didn't have time to flip through five different parenting books to remember where they agreed or disagreed on what to do.
projects.blurb: An offline, single-file compare-and-contrast of five well-known parenting books, built for the moment things are already going sideways. An interactive section lets you pick a position on each disagreement and copy out a decision summary.

projects.name: BitLock
projects.problem: I had a 10-button order-independent combination lock and no memory of the combination — 1,024 possibilities is too many to track by hand, especially with more than one person trying combos.
projects.blurb: A brute-force tracker for a 10-button combination lock. Shared state via Redis so multiple people can mark off attempted combinations from their own phones without duplicating work.

projects.name: Bearings
projects.problem: A group of us wanted to pinpoint something far away (a boat, a light, a sound) using nothing but our phones' compasses and GPS, without a rangefinder or a survey tool.
projects.blurb: A collaborative PWA: point your phone at a target, tap Record, and it combines bearings from multiple participants — using least-squares ray intersection — to triangulate the target's location on a map.

projects.name: Clear Skies Ahead
projects.problem: Standing under clouds (or in the sun), I wanted a quick answer to "how far do I need to go to change that" without squinting at a weather map.
projects.blurb: A PWA that reads your GPS location and compass bearing, then searches outward using live NOAA weather data — binary-searching down to the nearest half-mile — to tell you exactly how far to the nearest clear sky or nearest clouds.

projects.name: Ins-and-Outs
projects.problem: Our dog Madgy was recovering from a procedure and needed pills and bathroom trips tracked closely — across multiple people in the house, from memory, was not working.
projects.blurb: A quick-tap tracker for a recovering dog's pills, pees, and poos, so anyone in the house can log a moment in a couple of taps and everyone can see the latest status.
projects.repo_note: Built directly, no separate source repo to link.

projects.name: Ask the Stars
projects.problem: I wanted a way to reach an AI agent from places with no cell signal — backcountry trips, remote camping — where a normal app or chat client is useless.
projects.blurb: A personal AI agent reachable over satellite SMS, powered by Claude and Firebase. No app, no signal required — just a text message.
projects.live_note: SMS-based — there's no web page to link to.

projects.name: Kindling
projects.problem: Relationships need small, regular maintenance — check-ins, rituals, gestures — and those are exactly the things that quietly slip when life gets busy.
projects.blurb: A relationship-maintenance PWA for tracking the small habits that keep a relationship's spark alive.
projects.status_note: Build stalled partway through — not deployed yet.

projects.name: Spotter
projects.problem: During races and outdoor events, great photos of you get scattered across dozens of strangers' phones and never make it back to you.
projects.blurb: Crowdsourced, geotagged photo sharing for races and outdoor activities — so photos taken near you during an event are easy to find afterward.
projects.status_note: Deploys are currently failing — not live at the moment.
